scope: Local CPU observations, not universal timing or memory guarantees.
Cold runs use fresh workers and independent empty persistent caches.
Peak RSS is a process-lifetime high-water mark, including compilation.
Failed OOM observations retain checkpoint memory, which is not the final peak.
macOS and Linux use different JAX versions; their timings are not direct comparisons.
The macOS train and Linux benchmarks shared a physical host; elapsed times are not isolated hardware comparisons.
Numerical and conservation checks do not extend measured thermodynamic qualification.
No validated 3x cold-gradient speedup against v0.6.0 is claimed.
Normwise observations use infinity-norm backward errors and RHS-relative residual checks, and initialize the persistent cache before Fugacio imports.
Source digests distinguish numerical changes, runtime-setting metadata, and the completed-worker RSS guard. Every accepted observation has a recorded peak below its declared budget.
Prior numerical and resource failures retain their distinct source digests and implementation labels; they are not current acceptance claims.
The hard 7 GB optimization target does not apply to all sensitivity studies.

observations.name: ethanol-train-local-linux-vm-limit
observations.limitation: The watchdog allowed 12 GB, but the container had only 7.8 GB RAM plus 1.2 GB swap allowance and the VM had about 8.2 GB RAM plus 1.1 GB swap. This is not a test on a machine with 12 GB available to the worker.
